reconcile.note: Gill reads Luke's fright and John's gladness as one encounter, with Christ's wounds turning fear into joy.

discrepancy.note: Strauss notes the appearance narratives clash: Luke has the disciples terrified, supposing they saw a spirit, unlike John's glad reception.

quotes.text: and they, terrified at the sight, supposed that they saw a spirit.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), §139, on Luke 24:37.

sides.snippet: But they were terrified and filled with fear, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.
sides.verseText: But they were terrified and filled with fear, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.

sides.snippet: The disciples therefore were glad when they saw the Lord.
sides.verseText: When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad when they saw the Lord.
